label: November 9–15
title: “There Is No Other God That Can Deliver” —  Daniel 1

items.text: We can all benefit from the examples of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who faced great temptations to abandon their beliefs. They remained true to their covenants by doing small and simple things like praying, fasting, choosing good friends, trusting in God, and being a light to others. Their faith inspires believers to this day.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: In a sense, we all live in Babylon, often facing temptations to compromise our standards. As we read about Daniel and his friends, we can note how they responded to pressure and the results of their faith. Their experiences can help us trust in the Lord when we face opposition, even if miracles don't immediately follow.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Savior invites all to come unto Him and partake of His goodness. When teaching, ponder ways to give everyone an opportunity to participate. Don’t pressure anyone, but offer chances to share insights from scriptures, conference messages, or hymns, allowing the Spirit to guide their contributions and deepen understanding.

items.text: Daniel’s vision foretold future worldly kingdoms and the future kingdom of God, which “shall never be destroyed.” Elder D. Todd Christofferson taught that the Church is this prophesied latter-day kingdom, set up by God and rolling forth to fill the earth. Consider your role in helping this prophecy come to pass.

Receiving revelation requires spiritual preparation. Daniel's actions, such as praying and seeking God’s help, demonstrate how to approach Him. God prepared Daniel, and His help is available to us as we follow His counsel. Learn from Daniel’s words and actions to understand how to receive and act upon divine guidance.

Jesus Christ is the Son of the Eternal Father. The title 'Son of man' from Daniel 7:13 was understood by many Jews to refer to the coming Messiah. Ponder what these scriptures teach us about the Messiah and His divine relationship with the Eternal Father, recognizing His unique role and eternal significance.

When faced with moral dilemmas, Daniel and his friends chose to stand firm in their faith. By refusing to compromise their standards, even when threatened with severe punishment, they demonstrated profound trust in God’s power to deliver them. Their unwavering commitment serves as a powerful example for us today.

The Lord can work miracles in our lives when we exercise faith, even in seemingly impossible circumstances. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego’s deliverance from the fiery furnace was a testament to their faith and God’s power. This bears witness that there is no other God that can deliver like Him.

Righteous choices can lead others to greater faith in the Lord. When Daniel and his friends remained true to their convictions, their actions bore witness of God’s power and truth. Their example encouraged those around them to acknowledge the God of Israel, highlighting the influence of faithful discipleship.

Even when facing daunting challenges and cultural pressures, Daniel and his companions chose to honor their covenants. They understood that their strength came from God. By consistently turning to Him in prayer and righteous living, they were able to stand as lights in a challenging world.
